title: Why Can Horses Sleep Standing Up? 🐴
description:
Horses sleep standing up thanks to the stay apparatus, a set of tendons and ligaments that locks their legs, while the kneecap hooks over a ridge on the thighbone. But for deep REM sleep, a horse still has to lie down.

topic: Why can horses sleep standing up?
script: You'd topple in seconds, but a 500-kilo horse sleeps standing for hours. The secret is a lock, built right into its legs. It's called the stay apparatus, a web of tendons and ligaments that holds the joints straight with almost no muscle effort. The back leg is even cleverer. The kneecap slides up and hooks over a ridge on the thighbone, so the leg locks like a kickstand. The horse leans on that leg, tips the other hoof, and dozes. If a predator shows up, it's already on its feet. But that's only light sleep. To dream, a horse has to lie down, because its muscles go totally slack. It needs about half an hour of that a day. So would you rather lie down to dream, or sleep standing up, like a horse?
key_facts: stay apparatus locks the legs with almost no muscle effort
hind leg: patella hooks over the medial trochlear ridge of the femur
at least ~25-30 min REM a day; about 5-7 h total sleep
